doc.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021

title: The forthcoming Bill Evans book and the Peter Erskine story
summary: He explains writing a book with Charles Levin and tells how Peter Erskine joined Kenton at Newport.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Okay. Well here’s an opportunity to talk about your upcoming book, for a moment.
What made you decide to do it, and what can we expect to learn about Bill Evans? You don’t have to give away all your good stuff but —

Oh that’s okay, I don’t mind sharing a couple of things. But the reason I wanted to do it was because these stories were fresh in my mind starting in, you know, 1980 after he passed. And I just kept re-experiencing them and mulling them over. So sometime in the ‘90s I started to write them down. And then they were just kind of compiling and I would have different episodes of things. And when I had enough material together I reached out to one of my former graduate students who was older, Charles Levin. And Charles for 25 years was a newspaper journalist so he had experience in the field of writing. And we started working on this together and it started to really take shape and so now we’re at a point where it’s really, I think it’s going to be something worthwhile for people to read. There’s a lot of anecdotes about Bill that I share from my personal experience with him because I actually spent time living with him in his apartment from time to time you know. And we were on the road a lot, and things that I had seen and also we were able to track down witnesses, you know people that were actually there when I describe an event for example. I’ll give you an example. Here’s one that I don’t mind sharing because it’s with a buddy of mine, Peter Erskine. So when I was on Woody’s band, in 1972 we played the Newport Jazz Festival in New York. It was called Reunion at Newport. Alan Broadbent had written a feature tune with that title and it was featuring Stan Getz and Al Cohn and Zoot Sims and Chubby Jackson. I think was Red Norvo there, I can’t remember. A number of people that were in Woody’s bands over the years, right? So that was our segment. I went backstage and I see this skinny kid with long hair, he’s 19 years old and we meet and it’s Peter Erskine. And I say, “What are you doing?” He says, “I’m playing with Stan Kenton.” I says, “Well how long you been with the band?” He said, “Tonight’s my first night.” So what happened with Peter was he had been hired to play with June Christy. Nobody knew who he was, not even the guys in Kenton’s band, right? So Peter shows up, long hair, nobody knows him. He sight reads all of June’s stuff perfectly. They do the gig, he does a fantastic job, and right after the gig Stan says, you know, “Have your bags packed tomorrow morning” you know, “meet us in front of this hotel.” That was actually a fun recollection and I was able to get Peter to describe it from his perspective, and he did a great job.
That’s interesting, almost like a reporter who needs to get confirmation about their stories.

Well that is one Charles’s strengths because he’s very good at investigative journalism. He’s very good at tracking people down and he’s very good at conducting the interviews and getting the correct information, for what we need.
